item.title: Nearly all transgender youth satisfied with hormone therapy
item.description: A vast majority of transgender and gender-diverse youth in the United States are satisfied with their choice of gender-affirming hormone therapy. This emerges from a survey of nearly 400 transgender and gender-diverse youth, the largest survey of its kind to date. About 97 percent said it was the right decision. item.title: Climbers rescue orphaned seal pup from cliff on Kythira
item.description: On the Greek island of Kythira, climbers discovered an orphaned seal pup at the base of a cliff on the inaccessible Kalamia Beach during a hiking trip. The animal, a critically endangered Mediterranean monk seal, had likely been separated from its mother by a large wave near a nearby sea cave. The climbers safely placed the pup in a backpack...

item.title: Tokyo tackles waste problem with smart trash bins
item.description: Japan is known for the absence of public trash bins, by design: difficult-to-dispose waste would make people less inclined to create litter, and prevents overflowing bins. For tourists, however, this is confusing and frustrating. Tokyo removed all trash bins from the metro in 2022. At the same time, cities like Tokyo and Kyoto are working with companies on smarter solutions....

item.title: PFAS levels in English rivers fall 30%, in fish even 49%
item.description: Two banned 'forever chemicals', PFOA and PFOS, are being found in much lower concentrations in English rivers and fish. Research by the UK Environment Agency shows a decline of 29% for PFOA and 30% for PFOS in water, and even 49% in fish tissue. The substances were used for decades in water-repellent, flame-retardant and non-stick products, but were banned under...

item.title: Neupulse wristband nearly halves Tourette tics in British trial
item.description: A clinical trial in the United Kingdom involving 121 participants showed that wearing a prototype wristband device, Neupulse, reduced the frequency of tics by an average of 25 percent. item.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object ever to travel, reaches a new milestone on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. ET: a distance of one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles, after 49 years, two months and 11 days of travel. item.title: World premiere: bone marrow transplant cures aplastic anemia
item.description: A Catholic healthcare system in the American Midwest, Franciscan Health, has successfully completed the world's first reported bone marrow transplant for a non-malignant disease. Doctors used bone marrow from a deceased organ donor to treat a 40-year-old woman with aplastic anemia. After ten years of illness and multiple failed treatments, she underwent a stem cell transplant on April 18. Six...

item.title: Holiday friends David and Jodie married after 32 years
item.description: In 1994, David from Newcastle and Jodie met as teenagers during a holiday on the Greek island of Kos. They exchanged addresses and became pen pals, writing letters to each other for years. Then they lost touch, until David spotted a message from Jodie on his mother's phone twenty years later. item.description: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky has donated $100 million to San Francisco's parks, the largest gift from an individual donor in the city's history. item.title: SpaceX catches Starship with mechanical arms and makes history
item.description: SpaceX has for the first time caught a Starship spacecraft with mechanical arms at its launch facility in Texas, 22 hours after launch. According to the company, this demonstrates Starship's full reusability, intended for trips to the moon and Mars. The first-stage booster exploded shortly after launch on Friday, preventing the hoped-for double catch. SpaceX had previously successfully caught a...

item.title: Couple with autism and ADHD clean dirty street signs in Brighton
item.description: Paul and Ruth Richmond-Watson from Brighton, England, have been cleaning dirty street signs in East Sussex since September. The couple, both autistic with ADHD, were looking for a hobby to do together. Paul (47), originally from New Zealand and a former window cleaner, and Ruth (25) clean at least one sign per day, which takes each 20 to 25 minutes...

item.title: Ada Le Poidevin hid British soldiers from Nazis on Guernsey
item.description: The heroic wartime deeds of British shopkeeper Ada Le Poidevin have come to light 40 years after her death. During the Second World War, she and her husband Walter hid three British commandos — corporal Dennis Dumper, soldier Fred Drain and soldier Andrew Ross — in their garden shed on Nazi-occupied Guernsey, despite German troops living next door. item.title: Atolls Bikar and Bokak become new marine reserve
item.description: In the Marshall Islands, the coral atolls Bikar and Bokak have been designated as part of the country's first national marine reserve. Scientists describe the two remote atolls, located between Hawaii and the Philippines, as one of the last virtually pristine ecosystems in the world. item.description: Rick Addante from Palm Bay, Florida, rescued his vulnerable neighbors during a flood he himself described as 'biblical'. item.title: PolyGone Systems microplastics filter launches in Atlantic City
item.description: A water treatment facility in Atlantic City, New Jersey, has become the first in the world to be equipped with a system that removes microplastics from wastewater before it enters the ocean. item.title: China switches on world's largest liquid-air battery
item.description: In China's Qinghai province, the world's largest demonstration facility for liquid-air energy storage (LAES) has been put into operation. The installation uses green electricity to compress air to extreme density, after which it becomes liquid at approximately -190°C.
